source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact tab-separated Greek payload, retaining whitespace and variant markers.

key_decisions.rationale: Retain enslaved status and the partial claim on the produce rather than imply the whole harvest was owed.
key_decisions.before: At harvest time he sent a servant to the tenants to receive some of the vineyard’s fruit from them.
key_decisions.after: At harvest time he sent a slave to the tenants to collect his share of the vineyard's fruit.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And at the season he sent a servant to the tenants to receive from the tenants some of the fruit of the vineyard.

key_decisions.rationale: Retain the specific head injury without adding stoning from a variant.
key_decisions.before: Again the owner sent another servant. They struck this one on the head and treated him shamefully.
key_decisions.after: He sent another slave to them. They struck this one on the head and treated him shamefully.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And again he sent to them another servant; and that one they struck on the head and dishonored.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserve Mark's order of killing before expulsion rather than harmonize with other accounts.
key_decisions.before: So they seized him, killed him, and threw him out of the vineyard.
key_decisions.after: They seized him, killed him, and threw him out of the vineyard.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And taking him, they killed him and threw him out of the vineyard.

key_decisions.rationale: Retain the stone quotation and its rejected-to-central movement, with lineation distinguishing cited poetry.
key_decisions.before: Have you not read this Scripture: ‘The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone;
key_decisions.after: Have you not read this scripture? ‘The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: Have you not read this scripture: ‘The stone that the builders rejected, this has become the cornerstone;

key_decisions.rationale: Render the face-looking idiom as partiality and preserve both forms of the pressing tax question.
key_decisions.before: They came and said, “Teacher, we know that you are truthful and do not show favoritism. You do not judge by outward status but teach the way of God in truth. Is it lawful to pay tribute to Caesar or not?
key_decisions.after: They came and said, “Teacher, we know you are truthful and are not swayed by anyone, because you do not favor people according to their standing. You teach God's way truthfully. Is it lawful to pay the tax to Caesar or not? Should we pay it or should we not?”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And coming, they said to him, “Teacher, we know that you are true and do not care for anyone, for you do not look at the face of people, but teach the way of God in truth. Is it lawful to give tribute to Caesar, or not?

key_decisions.rationale: Preserve the give-back verb and balanced claims without making the saying a complete theory of government.
key_decisions.before: Jesus told them, “Give back to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s.” And they were amazed at him.
key_decisions.after: Jesus told them, “Give back to Caesar what belongs to Caesar, and to God what belongs to God.” They were amazed at him.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And Jesus said to them, “The things of Caesar give back to Caesar, and the things of God to God.” And they were amazed at him.

key_decisions.rationale: Retain when they rise, present in the pinned source despite variant markers, and the basis of the question.
key_decisions.before: In the resurrection, when they rise, whose wife will she be? All seven had married her.”
key_decisions.after: In the resurrection, when they rise, whose wife will she be? All seven had married her.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: In the resurrection, when they rise, whose wife will she be? For the seven had her as wife.”

key_decisions.rationale: Preserve the two marriage expressions and comparison rather than say people become angels.
key_decisions.before: When people rise from the dead, they neither marry nor are given in marriage but are like angels in heaven.
key_decisions.after: When people rise from the dead, they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like angels in heaven.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: For when they rise from the dead, they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like angels in the heavens.

key_decisions.rationale: Retain Israel's address and the confession's one-language, with a note on the alternate construction.
key_decisions.before: Jesus answered, “The first is: ‘Hear, Israel: The Lord our God, the Lord is one.
key_decisions.after: Jesus answered, “The first is, ‘Hear, Israel: the Lord our God, the Lord is one.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: Jesus answered, “The first is, ‘Hear, Israel: The Lord our God, the Lord is one;

key_decisions.rationale: Keep the scribe's three-term wording distinct from verse 30 and retain both kinds of sacrificial language.
key_decisions.before: And to love him with all the heart, all the understanding, and all the strength, and to love one’s neighbor as oneself, is more than all burnt offerings and sacrifices.”
key_decisions.after: To love him with all your heart, all your understanding, and all your strength, and to love your neighbor as yourself, matters more than all burnt offerings and sacrifices.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: and to love him from the whole heart and from the whole understanding and from the whole strength, and to love the neighbor as oneself, is more than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices.”

key_decisions.rationale: Preserve the Spirit attribution, two distinct lord referents, and beneath your feet rather than importing footstool.
key_decisions.before: David himself said by the Holy Spirit, ‘The Lord said to my Lord, Sit at my right hand until I put your enemies under your feet.’
key_decisions.after: David himself said by the Holy Spirit: ‘The Lord said to my lord, “Sit at my right until I put your enemies beneath your feet.”’
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: David himself said by the Holy Spirit, ‘The Lord said to my Lord, Sit at my right hand, until I put your enemies under your feet.’

key_decisions.rationale: Keep the predatory metaphor and religious pretense together, with stronger judgment as the stated result.
key_decisions.before: devour widows’ houses, and make long prayers for appearance. They will receive a greater judgment.”
key_decisions.after: They devour widows' houses and make long prayers for show. They will receive a harsher judgment.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: who devour widows’ houses and for appearance make long prayers. These will receive greater judgment.”

key_decisions.rationale: Resolve the unnamed subject and retain the manner of giving and large gifts without assigning a motive.
key_decisions.before: Jesus sat down opposite the treasury and watched how the crowd put money into it. Many rich people put in large amounts.
key_decisions.after: Jesus sat opposite the treasury and watched how the crowd put money into it. Many rich people put in large amounts.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And sitting opposite the treasury, he was watching how the crowd was putting money into the treasury; and many rich people were putting in much.

key_decisions.rationale: Keep two coins and the ancient comparison rather than convert to modern money or erase the narrator's explanation.
key_decisions.before: Then a poor widow came and put in two small copper coins, worth very little.
key_decisions.after: Then a poor widow came and put in two small copper coins, together worth a quadrans.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And one poor widow came and put in two small copper coins, which make a quadrans.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserve the paradoxical more and attention to the widow without adding a command to imitate her.
key_decisions.before: Jesus called his disciples and said, “Truly I tell you, this poor widow has put in more than all the others putting money into the treasury.
key_decisions.after: Jesus called his disciples over and said, “Truly I tell you, this poor widow has put in more than everyone else who gave to the treasury.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And calling his disciples to him, he said to them, “Truly I say to you, this poor widow has put in more than all those putting into the treasury.

key_decisions.rationale: Retain surplus/poverty and the final totality; do not soften all she had or decide the passage's evaluation in the text.
key_decisions.before: They all gave out of their abundance, but she, out of her poverty, put in everything she had—all she had to live on.”
key_decisions.after: They all gave out of their surplus, but she, out of her poverty, put in everything she had—her whole livelihood.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: For they all put in out of their abundance, but she out of her poverty put in everything she had, her whole life.”
